notes: TBox subject insert. 'An 1870-S three-dollar piece is a three-dollar piece', 'the three-dollar piece was a gold coin', 'an 1870-S coin bears the S mint mark' and 'S-mint-mark coins were struck at San Francisco' are firm class rules (the first and third come from the name, stated as chain steps in the record since 2026-10-31; the others are bridges). Since 2026-10-31 q2 ('only one known?') is determinate 'no' and w1 stores only the count (FINDINGS A1), so the two worlds differ only on q3's count and carry no axioms; q2 and q3 are fol arithmetic in the record. Relations once declared in this file are catalogued in RELATIONS.md since 2026-10-30.

halvard_coin: a coin from the Halvard find

queries.not_checked: fol (arithmetic): 'only one known' is a count (the record's answer is no: the find adds a newly found piece)

fol.notes: TBox subject insert. Coins are an uninterpreted sort, the classes Bool predicates. The edit is the class axiom plus what the record's chain marks as edit: the find holds a coin (halvard_1, a Skolem constant), newly found, so not the piece already known (known_piece). q2 ('only one known?') is asked of the members, as the chain reasons ('so at least two are known'): the stored uniqueness claim is a closed-world presupposition the insert gives up in every world (top-level gives_up, as the record's determinacy_why says no world keeps it). q3 is the count: w1 stores it as a figure (number_known), w2 the counting rule over the named coins (each counted once; halvard_2 names a possible second coin of the find, so the count rests on the prompt's 'one coin' and the named_only closure); the prompt gives the find's size (one coin, halvard_1).

one_known.says: One 1870-S three-dollar piece is known to exist. (stored)

only_one.says: Only one 1870-S three-dollar piece is known to exist: every known one is that piece. (stored closed list, before the find)

named_only.says: Every 1870-S three-dollar piece the model knows of is the one already known or a coin of the Halvard find. (closed world)

stores: number_known(three_dollar_1870s) == count(piece_1870s(known_piece), And(piece_1870s(halvard_1), known_piece != halvard_1), And(piece_1870s(halvard_2), known_piece != halvard_2, halvard_1 != halvard_2))

one_coin.says: The Halvard find holds one coin.
